- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 periods later.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias — reduce forecast toward historical mean (last 10–15 days) by 1–2% per period.
- If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative (e.g., 0.67 → -0.33 within 3 days), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–4% in next 2–3 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment; apply a 1–2% dampening factor if sentiment is erratic or mixed.
